theme: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
queries_run: gh search repos "opensky network dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "flight schedules dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "airline seat capacity route" --sort stars
WebSearch: github BTS T-100 airline market data python download repository (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)
WebSearch: github aviationstack airline route capacity seats dataset repository (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)

candidates.name: ADS-B-Exchange-Samples
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts + processed data converting ADS-B Exchange 'trace' JSON files (from samples.adsbexchange.com) into flattened CSV. Repo description says flight trace CSVs + metadata organized by date/ICAO tail number. Small hobby repo (0 stars), single contributor, updated Jan 2026.
candidates.why_useful: A worked method to turn ADS-B Exchange's free sample traces into per-flight CSV records (route, altitude, timestamps) -- could be adapted to proxy point-to-point flight volumes for gap #10 (airline/rail capacity) without needing an aviationstack key.
candidates.time_coverage: Unclear, likely a short recent window (ADS-B Exchange free samples only)

candidates.name: adsb-hist-snapshots-2025-08
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed ADS-B Exchange readsb-hist snapshots for August 2025, described as a JSON dataset -- appears to be raw historical position/state-vector dumps for that single month.
candidates.why_useful: A rare case of someone actually committing a month of raw ADS-B Exchange history to a repo rather than just scraping live; could be mined for a snapshot of US/global flight density in Aug 2025 as one data point for capacity gap #10, though a single month has limited standalone value.
candidates.geography: Unspecified (global feed, likely ADS-B Exchange worldwide coverage)
candidates.size_hint: Unknown, likely large raw JSON given readsb-hist format

candidates.name: adsb-tools
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scripts to download and filter ADS-B Exchange's daily flight dumps (their public bulk JSON feed of aircraft state vectors). Apache-2.0, 11 stars.
candidates.why_useful: A clean, small, working client for pulling ADS-B Exchange's daily global flight-position dumps -- the raw material needed to build airport-level departure/arrival counts as a travel-capacity proxy (gap #10), without needing a paid FlightRadar24/aviationstack key.
candidates.time_coverage: Daily dumps as available from ADS-B Exchange (pull-time only, not historical archive)
candidates.size_hint: Script only, no committed data (each daily dump is large raw JSON)

candidates.name: flight-tracer
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package for fetching, processing, storing, and plotting flight data from ADS-B Exchange. CC0-1.0 licensed, 18 stars, actively updated (Mar 2026).
candidates.why_useful: More mature/maintained acquisition tool than the other ADS-B Exchange scripts found here; CC0 license means output data could be freely stored point-in-time. Useful base for building a repeatable airport-traffic nowcast series (gap #10) if the team wants to start collecting ADS-B snapshots going forward.
candidates.geography: Global (ADS-B Exchange coverage, configurable by user)

candidates.name: opensky-traffic-viz
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tools to load and visualize OpenSky Network air traffic data (OpenSky's REST/Impala historical database of ADS-B flight records going back to ~2019, covering scheduled and general aviation traffic globally). MIT licensed, 11 stars.
candidates.why_useful: OpenSky Network's underlying historical database (queried through this or similar clients) is one of the few genuinely long-run, free, global flight-position archives -- a route-level or airport-level flight-count series derived from it could serve as an airline capacity/traffic proxy for gap #10. This particular repo is just a viz/loading helper, not the data itself, so it is a pointer to the acquisition method rather than a dataset.
candidates.geography: Global (OpenSky Network sensor coverage, strongest in Europe/US)
candidates.time_coverage: OpenSky historical DB extends back to ~2019 (not committed in this repo; queried live)
candidates.size_hint: Tool only; underlying OpenSky database is very large (external, queried via API)

candidates.name: local-flight-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Open air-traffic map application combining ADS-B Exchange and OpenSky Network data feeds for local/regional flight tracking. MIT licensed, 1 star, updated Sep 2026 (actively maintained).
candidates.why_useful: Combines both major free flight-tracking sources (ADS-B Exchange + OpenSky) in one client, which could be a starting point for a lightweight airport-departure-count scraper if the team wanted a point-in-time capacity series; marginal on its own since it's built for live map display, not data export.
candidates.geography: Configurable/local (whatever region the user points it at)

candidates.name: feedclient
candidates.what_it_holds: Official ADS-B Exchange feeder client (feeds an existing readsb/dump1090/piaware receiver INTO ADS-B Exchange), 102 stars, MIT license, actively updated (Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Not a data-pull tool -- it's for contributing ground-station data TO ADS-B Exchange, so it does not help acquire flight data for the pitch. Flagged only because it is the highest-starred, most-maintained repo in the ADS-B Exchange ecosystem and confirms the network is alive and growing (context for evaluating other ADS-B Exchange client repos above).

candidates.name: fr24scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Realtime FlightRadar24 scraper, 0 stars, updated Sep 2026 (very new/unproven).
candidates.why_useful: A candidate method for pulling FlightRadar24 route/schedule data if ADS-B Exchange/OpenSky prove insufficient, but it is unmaintained/unproven (0 stars, brand new) and scraping FlightRadar24 directly likely runs into the same terms-of-service question flagged for Airbnb scraping -- would need a human ToS call before any use.
candidates.size_hint: Small scraper script, no committed data

notes: This theme searched thin on gh search repos: 'opensky network dataset' and 'airline seat capacity route' and 'flight schedules dataset' returned zero or irrelevant (BI-dashboard tutorial) hits -- there is no committed BTS T-100/DB1B mirror, no aviationstack sample-data repo, and no seat-capacity-by-route dataset surfaced by keyword search in the 6-call budget. The ADS-B Exchange ecosystem is large but dominated by live feeder/tracker tools (feedclient, adsb-exchange setup scripts, map apps, home-automation integrations) rather than committed historical datasets; the few dataset-shaped repos found (JesanNJ samples, RedEye-adsb Aug-2025 snapshots) are small, single-purpose, and unmaintained. WebSearch was unavailable for this scout (session budget of 200 already exhausted by other agents before this call), so BTS T-100/DB1B, Eurocontrol, and aviationstack-specific searches that gh search repos handles poorly were not completed -- a follow-up scout with WebSearch budget should specifically target: 'BTS T-100 domestic market data github', 'Eurocontrol traffic data github', 'aviationstack sample github', 'openskynetwork opensky-api' (the official OpenSky Python client, well known but not confirmed in this run), and 'DB1B github mirror'. None of the candidates found here are committed, long, point-in-time datasets that would fill gap #10 outright -- all are acquisition methods of medium-or-lower confidence; the strongest is henriklied/adsb-tools or stiles/flight-tracer as a starting point for the team to build its own point-in-time airport-traffic series going forward, not a ready-made backfill.
